anchors.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Scope Garcia-Diaz’s JAK1/JAK2–STAT1/2/3–IRF1 mechanism to melanoma experiments; verify rather than repeat a mainly-STAT1 simplification.
anchors.supportingExcerpt: The sequence proposed by Taube and colleagues and mapped in more detail since is a loop. A T cell recognises a tumour peptide on HLA and releases interferon gamma; the interferon acts through the Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 in nearby tumour and immune cells; PD-L1 rises; PD-L1 binds PD-1 on the T cell and damps it. In melanoma cell lines, Garcia-Diaz and colleagues found that the interferon gamma, JAK1 and JAK2, STAT1, STAT2 and STAT3, IRF1 axis primarily regulates PD-L1, with IRF1 binding the PD-L1 promoter, and biopsies from patients with melanoma showed enrichment of that interferon signature and of STAT and IRF1 target genes in tumours that responded to anti-PD-1 treatment.
